newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pick concern as police seize fake salamis.
newsitem.headline: Pick concern as police seize fake salamis.

text.p: Meat processor Pick Szeged Rt expressed concern on Thursday that Hungary's domestic market may suffer from a rash of cheap imitations after police confiscated 800 sticks of fake Pick salami in raids this week.

"We are not so much concerned at the material cost to the company but rather at the risk of losing the trust of our customers," Pick CEO Vilmos Bihari told Reuters, adding that the cost in lost sales so far was around two million forints ($10,100).

Police made the discoveries on Tuesday in swoops on 11 shops in three of Budapest's main shopping centres. The raids had been prepared for two months in advance in collaboration with officials from Pick and the Consumer Protection Authority.
Bihari said several times more fake Pick salamis were likely to be in circulation and more raids would be organised around Hungary.
"We will focus on regions where tourism is stronger," he said. "We want to avoid losing trust among our foreign consumers."

Bihari said that while some of the imitations may find their way across the borders to neighbouring countries, he had no evidence of any being found on Pick's most important export market, Germany, which accounts for three-quarters of the company's foreign sales.
Pick exports around 40 percent of its products.

In the first quarter, Pick reported total sales rising to 6.68 billion forints from 5.94 billion, and Bihari indicated earlier to reuters that first half consolidated results due in August would confirm the upward trend.
The comments boosted Pick shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange to a new high of 15,250 on Thursday.
-- Duncan Shiels, Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040 ($ = 196.1 Hungarian Forints)
